source: While measuring silencing loss in diploids, we noticed that a wild-type diploid with one copy of HMLα::cre and the RFP-GFP cassette showed considerably reduced colony sectoring and a fourfold decrease (p = 1 × 10−5; Student's t test) in the frequency of half-sectored colonies in comparison to an isogenic haploid (Table 1), indicating a ploidy effect on the rate of RFP-to-GFP switching.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of haploid and diploid data.

claim: Colonies of the sir1, sir3 and sir4 hemizygotes showed a modest yet consistent increase in the number of green sectors compared to the wild-type diploid.
source: Compared to the wild-type diploid, colonies of the sir1, sir3 and sir4 hemizygotes showed a modest yet consistent increase in the number of green sectors (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1) and a higher occurrence of half sectors (Table 1 and Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 and Table 1.

claim: Colonies of the sir1, sir3 and sir4 hemizygotes showed a higher occurrence of half sectors compared to the wild-type diploid.
source: Compared to the wild-type diploid, colonies of the sir1, sir3 and sir4 hemizygotes showed a modest yet consistent increase in the number of green sectors (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1) and a higher occurrence of half sectors (Table 1 and Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 6B.

claim: Reducing the dose of the genes encoding Sir3 or Sir4, two structural components of heterochromatin, or Sir1, a protein that recruits these components, rendered silencing at HML less stable.
source: Therefore, reducing the dose of the genes encoding Sir3 or Sir4, two structural components of heterochromatin, or Sir1, a protein that recruits these components, rendered silencing at HML less stable.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the hemizygote data.

claim: Altered gene dosage of SIR1 and SIR4 also affects the silencing of a sensitized HMR::ADE2 allele (Sussel et al., 1993).
source: Altered gene dosage of SIR1 and SIR4 also affects the silencing of a sensitized HMR::ADE2 allele (Sussel et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Hemizygosity for SIR2 had no perceivable impact on colony sectoring.
source: Hemizygosity for SIR2 had no perceivable impact on colony sectoring (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sir2 is the only member of the sirtuin family of NAD+-dependent deacetylases previously shown to have a role in silencing at HML or HMR.
source: Sir2 is the only member of the sirtuin family of NAD+-dependent deacetylases previously shown to have a role in silencing at HML or HMR.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: Silencing is indistinguishable between wild type and mutants lacking any of the four HST genes as measured by mating efficiency (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
source: As measured by mating efficiency, silencing is indistinguishable between wild type and mutants lacking any of the four HST genes (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Hst3 and Hst4 have been shown to contribute to the silencing of subtelomeric genes (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
source: However, Hst3 and Hst4 have been shown to contribute to the silencing of subtelomeric genes (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008), as well as silencing of a URA3 reporter in a plasmid-borne HMR cassette (Grünweller and Ehrenhofer-Murray, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Hst3 and Hst4 contribute to silencing of a URA3 reporter in a plasmid-borne HMR cassette (Grünweller and Ehrenhofer-Murray, 2002).
source: However, Hst3 and Hst4 have been shown to contribute to the silencing of subtelomeric genes (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008), as well as silencing of a URA3 reporter in a plasmid-borne HMR cassette (Grünweller and Ehrenhofer-Murray, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Nicotinamide inhibits all five sirtuins in yeast (Imai et al., 2000; Landry et al., 2000a, 2000b; Smith et al., 2000; Tanner et al., 2000; Tanny and Moazed, 2001).
source: Since nicotinamide inhibits all five sirtuins in yeast (Imai et al., 2000; Landry et al., 2000a, 2000b; Smith et al., 2000; Tanner et al., 2000; Tanny and Moazed, 2001), we tested whether other sirtuins, in addition to Sir2, were involved in the nicotinamide-induced loss of silencing observed in Figure 2.

claim: Colonies of cells with HMLα::cre and the RFP-GFP cassette turned completely green in the absence of Sir2.
source: As expected, colonies of cells with HMLα::cre and the RFP-GFP cassette turned completely green in the absence of Sir2, a protein essential for the nucleation and maintenance of heterochromatin (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The colonies of hst1Δ, hst2Δ and hst4Δ mutants exhibited sectoring patterns that were indistinguishable from wild-type colonies.
source: The colonies of hst1Δ, hst2Δ and hst4Δ mutants exhibited sectoring patterns that were indistinguishable from wild-type colonies (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The hst3Δ mutant showed a striking increase in colony sectoring and a sevenfold greater frequency of half-sectored colonies compared to wild type.
source: In contrast, the hst3Δ mutant showed a striking increase in colony sectoring and a sevenfold greater frequency of half-sectored colonies compared to wild type (Table 1, Figure 7A,B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1, Figure 7A,B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Hst3 deacetylase contributed to the stability of silenced chromatin at HML.
source: Thus, the Hst3 deacetylase contributed to the stability of silenced chromatin at HML.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the hst3Δ mutant data.

claim: Silencing defects have not been detected at subtelomeric genes in either the hst3Δ or hst4Δ single mutant (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
source: Whereas silencing defects have not been detected at subtelomeric genes in either the hst3Δ or hst4Δ single mutant, the hst3Δ hst4Δ double mutant shows a measurable phenotype (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).

claim: The hst3Δ hst4Δ double mutant shows a measurable phenotype at subtelomeric genes (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
source: Whereas silencing defects have not been detected at subtelomeric genes in either the hst3Δ or hst4Δ single mutant, the hst3Δ hst4Δ double mutant shows a measurable phenotype (Brachmann et al., 1995; Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: It is likely that the deletion of HST4 would enhance the sectoring phenotype of the hst3Δ mutant.
source: Therefore, it is likely that the deletion of HST4 would enhance the sectoring phenotype of the hst3Δ mutant shown in Figure 7A.
evidence: This is based on inference from prior work on hst3Δ hst4Δ double mutants.

claim: Hst3 regulates the deacetylation of acetylated lysine 56 on histone H3 (H3 K56-ac) (Celic et al., 2006; Maas et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2008).
source: Hst3 regulates the deacetylation of acetylated lysine 56 on histone H3 (H3 K56-ac) (Celic et al., 2006; Maas et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Colonies of the K56Q mutant showed a dramatic increase in sectoring.
source: In our strains, with cre under the native α2 promoter at HML, colonies of the K56Q mutant showed a dramatic increase in sectoring, whereas the K56R mutant was similar to wild type (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Colonies of the K56R mutant were similar to wild type in sectoring pattern.
source: In our strains, with cre under the native α2 promoter at HML, colonies of the K56Q mutant showed a dramatic increase in sectoring, whereas the K56R mutant was similar to wild type (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7D.

claim: The histone H3 K56R substitution has previously been shown to decrease silencing under various conditions (Xu et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2011).
source: However, the histone H3 K56R substitution has previously been shown to decrease silencing under various conditions (Xu et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Cells expressing the H3 K56Q mutant produced similar patterns of colony sectoring regardless of whether Hst3 was present.
source: Cells expressing the H3 K56Q mutant produced similar patterns of colony sectoring regardless of whether Hst3 was present (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The H3 K56R substitution in hst3Δ cells restored silencing to wild-type levels, as determined by overall colony sectoring.
source: In addition, the H3 K56R substitution in hst3Δ cells restored silencing to wild-type levels, as determined by overall colony sectoring (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Blocking the acetylation of residue 56 suppressed the hst3Δ sectoring phenotype.
source: Therefore, blocking the acetylation of residue 56 suppressed the hst3Δ sectoring phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the H3 K56R hst3Δ data.

claim: The sectoring patterns suggested that Hst3 promoted the stability of silencing through the deacetylation of histone H3 K56-ac.
source: Collectively, the sectoring patterns suggested that Hst3 promoted the stability of silencing through the deacetylation of histone H3 K56-ac.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from hst3Δ and histone H3 K56 mutants.

claim: The deletion of HST3 caused a threefold increase in the half-sector frequency of wild type (p = 3 × 10−4; Student's t test).
source: Whereas the deletion of HST3 caused a threefold increase in the half-sector frequency of wild type (p = 3 × 10−4; Student's t test), it did not significantly affect the half-sector frequency of the H3 K56Q mutant (p = 0.3; Student's t test) or the surprisingly high half-sector frequency of the H3 K56R mutant (p = 0.06; Student's t test) (Table 1 and Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7D.

claim: The deletion of HST3 did not significantly affect the half-sector frequency of the H3 K56Q mutant (p = 0.3; Student's t test).
source: Whereas the deletion of HST3 caused a threefold increase in the half-sector frequency of wild type (p = 3 × 10−4; Student's t test), it did not significantly affect the half-sector frequency of the H3 K56Q mutant (p = 0.3; Student's t test) or the surprisingly high half-sector frequency of the H3 K56R mutant (p = 0.06; Student's t test) (Table 1 and Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7D.

claim: The deletion of HST3 did not significantly affect the surprisingly high half-sector frequency of the H3 K56R mutant (p = 0.06; Student's t test).
source: Whereas the deletion of HST3 caused a threefold increase in the half-sector frequency of wild type (p = 3 × 10−4; Student's t test), it did not significantly affect the half-sector frequency of the H3 K56Q mutant (p = 0.3; Student's t test) or the surprisingly high half-sector frequency of the H3 K56R mutant (p = 0.06; Student's t test) (Table 1 and Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7D.

claim: The state of histone H3 K56 affected the stability of silencing at HML.
source: Thus, the state of histone H3 K56 affected the stability of silencing at HML, and amino acid substitutions of this residue were epistatic to the hst3Δ mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from hst3Δ and histone H3 K56 mutants.

claim: Amino acid substitutions of histone H3 K56 were epistatic to the hst3Δ mutation.
source: Thus, the state of histone H3 K56 affected the stability of silencing at HML, and amino acid substitutions of this residue were epistatic to the hst3Δ mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from hst3Δ and histone H3 K56 mutants.

claim: Colonies derived from cells in which the only source of histone H3–H4 genes was a plasmid-borne copy of HHT2-HHF2 exhibited more sectoring than colonies of cells containing both HHT1-HHF1 and HHT2-HHF2 at their native chromosomal loci.
source: Colonies derived from cells in which the only source of histone H3–H4 genes was a plasmid-borne copy of HHT2-HHF2 exhibited more sectoring than colonies of cells containing both HHT1-HHF1 and HHT2-HHF2 at their native chromosomal loci (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Silencing was likely affected by levels of histones H3 and H4 that were either limiting or improperly balanced with the levels of histones H2A and H2B.
source: Assuming the decrease in gene copy number led to a decrease in protein abundance, silencing was likely affected by levels of histones H3 and H4 that were either limiting or improperly balanced with the levels of histones H2A and H2B.
evidence: This is based on inference from the observation of increased sectoring with reduced histone gene copy number.

claim: Histone dosage has previously been shown to affect various functions of heterochromatin (Moore et al., 1979; Moore et al., 1983; Venditti et al., 1999).
source: Consistent with these possibilities, histone dosage has previously been shown to affect various functions of heterochromatin (Moore et al., 1979; Moore et al., 1983; Venditti et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The reduction from two copies of the histone H3–H4 gene pair to one copy enhanced the sectoring phenotype of hst3Δ colonies.
source: Whereas the reduction from two copies of the histone H3–H4 gene pair to one copy did enhance the sectoring phenotype of hst3Δ colonies (compare panels A and C in Figure 7 and panels A and B in Figure 7—figure supplement 1), it did not increase the half-sector frequency in the hst3Δ background as it did in the wild-type background (Table 1 and Figure 7B,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduction from two copies of the histone H3–H4 gene pair to one copy did not increase the half-sector frequency in the hst3Δ background as it did in the wild-type background.
source: Whereas the reduction from two copies of the histone H3–H4 gene pair to one copy did enhance the sectoring phenotype of hst3Δ colonies (compare panels A and C in Figure 7 and panels A and B in Figure 7—figure supplement 1), it did not increase the half-sector frequency in the hst3Δ background as it did in the wild-type background (Table 1 and Figure 7B,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7B,D.

claim: The degree to which histone H3–H4 gene dosage affected silencing, at least during the first cell division of colony growth, depended on the genetic background.
source: Therefore, the degree to which histone H3–H4 gene dosage affected silencing, at least during the first cell division of colony growth, depended on the genetic background.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of histone dosage effects in different genetic backgrounds.

claim: Most cells remained red throughout the duration of the time course in live-cell imaging.
source: Most cells remained red throughout the duration of the time course.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging.

claim: Rare RFP-to-GFP switches occurred in a subset of the lineages during live-cell imaging.
source: Consistent with the sectors observed within colonies, rare RFP-to-GFP switches occurred in a subset of the lineages (see Video 1 for an example).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging shown in Video 1.

claim: The rate of switching observed with live-cell imaging was within 10% of the rate of switching determined by the half-sector assay.
source: The rate of switching observed with live-cell imaging was within 10% of the rate of switching determined by the half-sector assay.
evidence: This is a comparison of data from two different experimental approaches.

claim: Silencing loss followed by recombination was not restricted to either the mother or daughter cell.
source: Multiple occurrences of both patterns 1 and 2 (Figure 8D) indicated that silencing loss followed by recombination was not restricted to either the mother or daughter cell (Given that pattern 3 was supported by only one example, we refrained from offering an interpretation of this event).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: It was likely that recombination of the loxP sites occurred prior to DNA replication in cells that had small buds when GFP fluorescence was first detected.
source: Since the bud emerges during early S phase, and there were no cases of only the mother or daughter cell remaining green following the onset of GFP expression in a small-budded cell (patterns 4 and 5), it was likely that recombination of the loxP sites occurred prior to DNA replication.
evidence: This is based on inference from the live-cell imaging data and knowledge of the cell cycle.

claim: Recombination may have occurred shortly after DNA replication at both newly synthesized copies of the RFP-GFP cassette in cells that had small buds when GFP fluorescence was first detected.
source: Alternatively, recombination may have occurred shortly after DNA replication at both newly synthesized copies of the RFP-GFP cassette.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation for the observed pattern.

claim: 8 of the 12 cells that expressed detectable GFP as large-budded cells gave rise to mother-daughter pairs in which only the mother or daughter remained green (patterns 7 and 8).
source: In contrast, 8 of the 12 cells that expressed detectable GFP as large-budded cells gave rise to mother-daughter pairs in which only the mother or daughter remained green (patterns 7 and 8) (Figure 8C,D), indicating that Cre catalyzed recombination after S phase and acted on only one of the two RFP-GFP cassettes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging shown in Figure 8C,D.

claim: Cre catalyzed recombination after S phase and acted on only one of the two RFP-GFP cassettes in cells that expressed detectable GFP as large-budded cells and gave rise to mother-daughter pairs in which only the mother or daughter remained green.
source: In contrast, 8 of the 12 cells that expressed detectable GFP as large-budded cells gave rise to mother-daughter pairs in which only the mother or daughter remained green (patterns 7 and 8) (Figure 8C,D), indicating that Cre catalyzed recombination after S phase and acted on only one of the two RFP-GFP cassettes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the live-cell imaging data.

claim: The time between recombination, which occurred some point after DNA replication, and GFP detection, which occurred when a large bud was present, spanned only a fraction of a complete cell cycle.
source: Switches that followed patterns 7 and 8 also demonstrated that the time between recombination, which occurred some point after DNA replication, and GFP detection, which occurred when a large bud was present, spanned only a fraction of a complete cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the live-cell imaging data.

claim: For three of the RFP-to-GFP switches, a second switch was observed in the daughter cell that arose from the immediately preceding cell division.
source: For three of the RFP-to-GFP switches, we observed a second switch in the daughter cell that arose from the immediately preceding cell division (Figure 8B,D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging shown in Figure 8B,D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Paired switches could have reflected either two loss-of-silencing events in directly related cells, or rather one loss-of-silencing event that happened when the mother cell and its daughter still shared a cytoplasm.
source: These paired switches, which occurred either simultaneously or within 40 min of each other, could have reflected either two loss-of-silencing events in directly related cells, or rather one loss-of-silencing event that happened when the mother cell and its daughter still shared a cytoplasm, assuming there was perdurance of the Cre protein in both cells and a delay in recombination.
evidence: This is based on inference and speculation from the live-cell imaging data.

claim: The incorporation of newly synthesized Sir3 into silenced chromatin during G1-phase arrest suggests that at least some Sir3 binding to nucleosomes is transient (Cheng and Gartenberg, 2000).
source: The incorporation of newly synthesized Sir3 into silenced chromatin during G1-phase arrest suggests that at least some Sir3 binding to nucleosomes is transient (Cheng and Gartenberg, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Fluorescence-recovery-after-photobleaching experiments have shown that heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1), a structural component of heterochromatin in other eukaryotes, can rapidly associate and dissociate from heterochromatic loci (Cheutin et al., 2003; Festenstein et al., 2003).
source: Similarly, fluorescence-recovery-after-photobleaching experiments have shown that heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1), a structural component of heterochromatin in other eukaryotes, can rapidly associate and dissociate from heterochromatic loci (Cheutin et al., 2003; Festenstein et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Heterochromatin dynamics had a functional impact on the transcriptional repression imparted by Sir proteins.
source: Here, we showed that heterochromatin dynamics had a functional impact on the transcriptional repression imparted by Sir proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from this study.

claim: Losses of silencing at HML and HMR resulted from stochastic fluctuations in the local concentration of silencing factors.
source: Perhaps losses of silencing at HML and HMR resulted from stochastic fluctuations in the local concentration of silencing factors.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed losses of silencing.

claim: Specific perturbations such as DNA replication may have disrupted the binding of Sir proteins to nucleosomes, thereby creating an opportunity for RNA polymerase to access heterochromatin.
source: Alternatively, specific perturbations such as DNA replication may have disrupted the binding of Sir proteins to nucleosomes, thereby creating an opportunity for RNA polymerase to access heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation for the observed losses of silencing.

claim: Sir1 may serve a purpose in the recovery of silencing on the rare occasion that it is lost.
source: Therefore, Sir1 may serve a purpose in the recovery of silencing on the rare occasion that it is lost.
evidence: This is based on inference from the finding that wild-type cells experience transient losses of silencing.

claim: The silenced subset of sir1Δ cells was fully repressed.
source: By directly measuring the transcription of a gene from the native α2 promoter at HML with single-cell and single-molecule resolution, we showed that the silenced subset of sir1Δ cells was fully repressed, whereas the expressed subset of sir1Δ cells transcribed cre to the level of sir4Δ cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-molecule RNA FISH.

claim: The expressed subset of sir1Δ cells transcribed cre to the level of sir4Δ cells.
source: By directly measuring the transcription of a gene from the native α2 promoter at HML with single-cell and single-molecule resolution, we showed that the silenced subset of sir1Δ cells was fully repressed, whereas the expressed subset of sir1Δ cells transcribed cre to the level of sir4Δ cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-molecule RNA FISH.

claim: Deletion of SIR1 affected the rate of silencing loss, but not the level of repression.
source: Deletion of SIR1 affected the rate of silencing loss, but not the level of repression since approximately half of all sir1 cells completely lacked cre transcripts.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined FISH and Cre-based assay data for sir1Δ cells.

claim: The persistence of RFP expression within regions of sir1Δ colonies underscored the remarkable ability of heterochromatin to template its own replication for multiple cell divisions.
source: Moreover, the persistence of RFP expression within regions of sir1Δ colonies containing either HMLα::cre or HMRα::cre and the RFP-GFP cassette underscored the remarkable ability of heterochromatin to template its own replication for multiple cell divisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of red sectors in sir1Δ colonies.

claim: The dynamic nature of silenced chromatin could result from stochastic processes intrinsic to, for example, the binding constants of Sir proteins for their nucleosomes and serve no useful role.
source: In principle, the dynamic nature of silenced chromatin could result from stochastic processes intrinsic to, for example, the binding constants of Sir proteins for their nucleosomes and serve no useful role.
evidence: This is a speculative possibility about the function of heterochromatin dynamics.

claim: The stability of silencing at HML and HMR could be tuned high enough to achieve cell-type specificity, yet just low enough to allow for events such as DNA replication or mating-type interconversion.
source: Alternatively, the stability of silencing at HML and HMR could be tuned high enough to achieve cell-type specificity, yet just low enough to allow for events such as DNA replication or mating-type interconversion.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative possibility about the function of heterochromatin dynamics.

claim: Successful mating-type switching requires that the invading MAT strand, along with the accessory proteins involved in recombinational repair, gain access to the heterochromatic donor sequence.
source: Therefore, successful switching requires that the invading MAT strand, along with the accessory proteins involved in recombinational repair, gain access to the heterochromatic donor sequence.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge about mating-type switching.

claim: The dynamics of silenced chromatin may contribute to the efficiency of mating-type interconversion.
source: We speculate that the dynamics of silenced chromatin may contribute to the efficiency of mating-type interconversion.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the function of heterochromatin dynamics.

claim: H3 K56 localizes to the DNA entry/exit region of the nucleosome (Luger et al., 1997).
source: H3 K56 localizes to the DNA entry/exit region of the nucleosome (Luger et al., 1997), and in the acetylated state it is thought to promote transient DNA 'breathing', during which the DNA partially unwraps from the nucleosome (Neumann et al., 2009; Simon et al., 2011; North et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: In the acetylated state, H3 K56 is thought to promote transient DNA 'breathing', during which the DNA partially unwraps from the nucleosome (Neumann et al., 2009; Simon et al., 2011; North et al., 2012).
source: H3 K56 localizes to the DNA entry/exit region of the nucleosome (Luger et al., 1997), and in the acetylated state it is thought to promote transient DNA 'breathing', during which the DNA partially unwraps from the nucleosome (Neumann et al., 2009; Simon et al., 2011; North et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: H3 K56-ac is important for transcriptional activation (Williams et al., 2008; Värv et al., 2010).

evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Telomeric heterochromatin is more accessible to the bacterial dam DNA methylase in various H3 K56 mutants (Xu et al., 2007).
source: Furthermore, H3 K56-ac is important for transcriptional activation (Williams et al., 2008; Värv et al., 2010), and telomeric heterochromatin is more accessible to the bacterial dam DNA methylase in various H3 K56 mutants (Xu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: H3 K56-ac destabilizes the nucleosome conformation and thereby renders the DNA more accessible to RNA polymerase.
source: Collectively, these observations suggest that H3 K56-ac destabilizes the nucleosome conformation and thereby renders the DNA more accessible to RNA polymerase.
evidence: This is based on inference from prior work on H3 K56-ac.

claim: H3 K56 acetylation peaks during S phase (Masumoto et al., 2005).
source: Whereas H3 K56 acetylation peaks during S phase (Masumoto et al., 2005), Hst3 expression does not peak until G2/M phase (Spellman et al., 1998; Celic et al., 2006; Maas et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Hst3 expression does not peak until G2/M phase (Spellman et al., 1998; Celic et al., 2006; Maas et al., 2006).
source: Whereas H3 K56 acetylation peaks during S phase (Masumoto et al., 2005), Hst3 expression does not peak until G2/M phase (Spellman et al., 1998; Celic et al., 2006; Maas et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Heterochromatin may be especially susceptible to transcription during the time after K56-acetylated histone H3 is deposited into chromatin, but before Hst3 removes the modification.
source: Therefore, heterochromatin may be especially susceptible to transcription during the time after K56-acetylated histone H3 is deposited into chromatin, but before Hst3 removes the modification.
evidence: This is based on inference from the cell cycle regulation of H3 K56 acetylation and Hst3 expression.

claim: The detection of a stability phenotype in the hst3 mutant underscored the importance of measuring fluctuations in repression for a fuller understanding of heterochromatin.
source: As previous measurements of HML silencing were unable to distinguish hst3 mutants from wild type, our detection of a stability phenotype in this mutant underscored the importance of measuring fluctuations in repression for a fuller understanding of heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of the Cre-based assay to previous assays.

claim: The Cre-based assay provides the opportunity to measure the effects of transient environmental or cellular stresses on silencing subsequent to their occurrence.
source: By preserving a historical record of transcription, the Cre-based assay also provides the opportunity to measure the effects of transient environmental or cellular stresses on silencing subsequent to their occurrence.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the Cre-based assay.

claim: The fold repression of α2 and cre did not significantly differ (p = 0.12; Student's t test).
source: The fold repression of α2 and cre did not significantly differ (p = 0.12; Student's t test).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from quantitative RT-PCR shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The fold repression of HMLα::cre did not significantly differ between the red and green samples (p = 0.43; Student's t test).
source: The fold repression of HMLα::cre did not significantly differ between the red and green samples (p = 0.43; Student's t test).
